mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances triggered by a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% within a month signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances triggered by a UNRATE decrease > 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances following a sustained increase in HOUST over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances triggered by a decrease in INDPRO > 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening consumer demand and labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances triggered by a joint increase in RSAFS and decrease in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, which can lead to monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances following a sustained increase in CPIAUCSL over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances triggered by a PAYEMS increase > 200,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances triggered by a decrease in GDPC1 > 0.5% in a quarter.
